rules.title: Two Genders (en / ett)
rules.explanation: Swedish nouns have one of two genders, **common** (en-words) or **neuter** (ett-words). You learn the gender together with the noun. The indefinite article shows it, **en** bil (a car) versus **ett** hus (a house). The adjective agrees too, en stor bil but ett stor**t** hus.
noticing_prompts: In en bil and ett hus, which little word signals the gender?
The adjective stor becomes stort with hus. What triggers the extra -t?
How can you tell whether a noun is an en-word or an ett-word?

structured_input.question: Why is it stort and not stor?
options: hus is a neuter (ett-word), so the adjective adds -t
structured_input.feedback: A neuter (ett-word) noun makes the adjective take -t, so stort.

structured_input.question: Which do you have? Choose the true one.
structured_input.feedback: bil and cykel are en-words (common), hus is an ett-word (neuter).

quiz.feedback_why: hus is a neuter noun, so it takes ett.
bil is a common (en) noun, so the adjective stays stor.

communicative_production.prompt: Name one en-word and one ett-word you own, each with an adjective.
communicative_production.model: Jag har en ny cykel och ett litet bord.
communicative_production.model_translation: I have a new bicycle and a small table.
communicative_production.hint: en-word keeps the plain adjective (ny), ett-word adds -t (litet).

rules.title: The Definite is a Suffix
rules.explanation: Swedish has **no separate word for the**. The definite form is a **suffix** on the noun. Common (en) nouns add **-en** (bok → bok**en**), neuter (ett) nouns add **-et** (hus → hus**et**). So en bok (a book) becomes bok**en** (the book).

context_dialogue.speaker: JON
context_dialogue.translation: The book is on the table.

noticing_prompts: bok means a book. What does boken mean?
Compare boken and huset. Which ending goes with an en-word, which with an ett-word?
Is there any separate word for the in these sentences?

structured_input.question: How is the house expressed here?
options: With the -et suffix on hus (an ett-word)
With a separate word before hus
hus is already definite by itself
structured_input.feedback: The definite is a suffix, and ett-words take -et, so huset.

structured_input.question: Which is on your table right now? Choose one.
structured_input.feedback: Each noun is in the definite form with -en or -et, boken, datorn, nyckeln.

quiz.feedback_why: The common (en) noun bok takes -en, so boken.
The neuter (ett) noun hus takes -et, so huset.

communicative_production.prompt: Say where two things are, using the definite form (-en / -et).
communicative_production.model_translation: The book is on the table.
